event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell with Tamsin's arm across her and Tamsin's curls in her mouth.
Tamsin wakes, sees where she is, and goes red from her collar to her hairline.

memory.fact: Tamsin fell asleep in Elsie's attic bed on the night of the eighth, and Elsie lay down beside her.

event: She says she only meant to read the notices; Elsie says she snores like a kettle, and laughs.

memory.fact: Tamsin snores like a little kettle in her sleep, and talks to trolls.
Tamsin snores like a little kettle in her sleep, and talks to trolls.

event: Tamsin laughs too, and stays lying there a while longer than she needs to.
Elsie waters the plants, and Tamsin solemnly says good morning to Sunny the lemon.
Downstairs the baker looks at Tamsin, then at Elsie, and raises one eyebrow.
Elsie buys two honey buns, and the baker adds a third for Tamsin unasked.

changes.note: Two honey buns at a pip each; the baker's third for Tamsin is free: 114 → 112

event: At the guild hall Tamsin goes straight to the E-rank board with her copied notices.
The clerk tells her a party takes only notices at the rank of its lowest member.
He says the guild raises an F-rank to E once she has done ten notices well.
Elsie counts on her fingers: rats, goat, moonbells, cat, cart, glowcaps; four more.
Tilly arrives with a pear fizz in each hand and asks what Elsie is counting.

changes.note: Bond: Tilly 30 → 31 (kindness: a pear fizz for Elsie)

event: Elsie says four more notices till E-rank, and Tilly squeaks and spills a fizz.
Cora comes out of the charcoal door, and Elsie asks if she slept well.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 20 → 21 (kindness: Elsie offers her a honey bun)

event: Cora says well enough; Elsie notices the lavender sprig is gone and her coat buttonhole is bare.
New on the F-rank board: eels at the Copper Baths, a glasshouse watch, festival fireworks.
Tamsin picks the eels at once, because eels can be hit.
The clerk enters the party for the eels, and Cora writes it in her ledger.
The Copper Baths sit under a green copper dome on the lake shore, steam curling from the vents.
A sign on the door says today is a women's day, and Tilly reads it twice and goes pink.
The bath-keeper, a stout woman in a rubber apron, takes them down to the boiler room.
She says Mere eels as long as a woman have got into the cistern and are fouling the pipes.
She says they bite hard and hold, but they're slow on land and hot water kills them.
Elsie asks if they can be driven out instead of killed; the keeper shrugs and says if you can.
An iron ladder goes down from the boiler room into the dark cistern.
Tilly looks down the ladder, and Elsie squeezes her hand and goes first.
The cistern is a brick vault knee-deep in cold water, with a grated outflow to the Mere.
Long dark shapes slide through the water round their legs, and Tilly clutches Elsie's arm.
Elsie says if they open the outflow and warm the water behind them, the eels will swim for the lake.
Tilly says she can brew warm; not killing warm, just nasty warm.
Tamsin wades to the outflow grate and hauls it open with a scream of rusted iron.
Tilly drops a fizzing vial into the far end, and the water there starts to steam.

changes.note: Tilly gains 10 XP for Brew in the field: the warming vial (100 → 110)

event: The eels stir and thrash and start for the open outflow.
One comes the wrong way, straight at Elsie's legs.
Cora steps in front of Elsie, and the eel bites her forearm and holds on.
Cora goes white and silent, her jaw set.
Tamsin grabs the eel behind the head and prises its jaws open with both thumbs.
Elsie takes the eel's tail end and together they carry it, writhing, to the outflow.
It shoots away to the Mere, and the last of the eels go after it.
Tamsin slams the grate shut, and Tilly's warm water swirls round their knees.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 21 → 24 (danger shared: steps between Elsie and the eel)
Bond: Tamsin 43 → 46 (danger shared: the eels in the cistern)
Bond: Tilly 31 → 34 (danger shared: the eels in the cistern)

event: Elsie turns to Cora, who is holding her arm against her coat.
Elsie says Cora stepped in front of her; Cora says it was her duty, and won't meet her eyes.
Up in the boiler room Elsie unbuttons Cora's sleeve and rolls it to the elbow.
The bite is a neat ring of punctures, bleeding slow; Elsie cleans it with salve from her satchel.
Cora's bare forearm is pale and fine-boned, and her pulse jumps under Elsie's thumb.
Elsie bandages it, slow and careful, and Cora watches her hands the whole time.
Elsie kisses the bandage, the way her mother did, and Cora goes very still.
Cora asks what that was for; Elsie says it helps a hurt mend, her mother swore by it.
The bath-keeper peers down the ladder, sees clean water, and whoops.
She pays them the notice on the spot, and Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly share it out.

changes.note: Her share of the four-lantern eel notice: 13 pips, 112 → 125
Tamsin's share of the eel notice: 13 pips, 114 → 127

event: A window opens in front of Elsie in the boiler room: Level up, and a new skill, Devotion.

changes.note: Elsie gains 40 XP for the eels in the cistern, driven out (130 → 170 / 150)
Tamsin gains 40 XP for the eels in the cistern (220 → 260)

event: Elsie gives Tilly the odd pips, and Cora writes it in her ledger one-handed.

changes.note: Tilly's share, 13 pips plus the odd pip Elsie gives her: 124 → 138

event: The keeper says it's a women's day, and they have earned the pools for nothing.
Tamsin is out of her jerkin before the keeper finishes speaking.
Cora says she is on duty, and will wait in the hall.
Elsie says Cora can watch her just as well from the pool, and takes her good hand.
Cora looks at the ledger, at Elsie, and lets herself be pulled along.
The great warm pool is green-tiled under the copper dome, full of steam and women's voices.
Elsie slips into the water in her shift, sighs, and floats on her back with her eyes shut.

changes.note: Elsie takes off her outfit and goes into the pool in her shift

event: Tamsin dives in and comes up beside her, and stares, and then looks very hard at the ceiling.
Tilly sits on the steps in her shift up to her chin, goggles still on her head, crimson.
Elsie paddles over and takes Tilly's goggles off and sets them on the side.
Elsie unbraids Tilly's singed braids and washes her hair, humming.
Tilly sits perfectly still under Elsie's hands with her eyes shut, breathing very carefully.
Tamsin swims slow lengths and keeps ending them near Elsie.
Cora comes out of the changing room last, in a long shift, her hair down to her waist.
Elsie calls across the pool that Cora's hair is beautiful, out loud, for everyone to hear.
Half the women in the pool turn to look, and Cora walks into the water to her shoulders.
Elsie swims to her and asks if the water stings her arm; Cora says it is only warm.
In the steam room the four of them sit on the slatted bench wrapped in towels.
Elsie sits between Tamsin and Cora, her damp shoulder touching both of theirs.
Tamsin's thigh presses against Elsie's under the towel, and Tamsin breathes like she has run.
Cora sits straight and still, and her bandaged arm rests a finger's width from Elsie's knee.
Tilly, opposite, says the steam is very hot, twice, fanning herself with both hands.
Elsie says she wants every morning to be like this one, and leans her head on Cora's shoulder.
Cora stops breathing, and then very slowly lets her head rest against Elsie's.
They plunge in the cold pool after, and Tilly shrieks so loud the keeper comes running.
Dressed again on the steps outside, Cora pins her hair back up, every strand.

changes.note: Elsie is dressed in her outfit again on the steps outside

event: Elsie says it's a shame, and Cora's ears turn pink.
Cora says she has her report to write, and goes, one hand on her bandage.
At the Tipsy Heron Tamsin pays for stew for the three of them, to celebrate eels.

changes.note: Tamsin buys stew for three at the Tipsy Heron: 12 pips, 127 → 115
Elsie ends the chapter with 125 pips: 12 lanterns, 5 pips
Tamsin ends the chapter with 115 pips
Tilly ends the chapter with 138 pips
Bond: Tamsin 46 → 47 (kindness: stew for the three of them)

event: Tilly says they're three notices from E now, and the blue house is four suns.
Tamsin says at four lanterns a notice that's a great many eels.
Elsie says then they'll be very good at eels, and Tilly laughs into her stew.
In the afternoon they walk by the blue-doored house on Willow Canal; the card is still up.
Elsie touches the blue door with two fingers, as if it's someone's hand.
Tamsin walks Tilly back to Pickle Row, and Elsie goes home along the canal alone.
In the attic Elsie writes in her notebook: Cora, stepped in front of me.
Under it she writes: Cora's hair down. Then she draws a little wobbly heart beside it.
At dusk the lamplighters' boats come by below the round window, one lantern at a time.
Elsie writes her mother about the baths, and Cora, and the eels they let go.
Down the Tether Tamsin is quiet and restless, as if she can't settle.
Elsie leans her head on the round window and hums until the restlessness eases.
